title: How token limits silently edit your input
text: This is Humanitarians. Models read tokens, not words, and can only take in so many. Feed a long document past the limit, and the rest is cut off, sometimes mid-thought. Hi, I'm Asavari, a fellow at Humanitarians AI. This video

title: The 512-token earnings statement sentiment bug
text: Is about a subtle bug that causes big mistakes. How a model's token limit can silently drop the one word that flips a sentence's meaning. title: Smart chunking: Keeping claims with qualifiers
text: Statement. The text says revenue grew, and then just past the cutoff, excluding one-time items. The model scores it as strong growth. It never saw the qualifier. title: Why larger context windows still have middle-attention blind spots
text: 512 tokens, splitting ideas in half. The better approach splits on meaning, keeping a claim with a qualifier that modifies it, and overlapping chunks so nothing important lands on a boundary. A warning, because people reach for the obvious fix. Newer models have larger windows, but every model still has a limit, and long documents still get truncated. Worse, even within the window, models pay less attention to the middle. A bigger window pushes the boundary out. It doesn't make it disappear. Know the token limit and how long your input really is. Look at where your chunks actually cut. Ask whether a qualifier could get separated from its claim, and check the tail of the document. The cutoff is a silent editor of your data. If you don't decide where it falls, it decides for you. The 512 token blind spot from Humanitarians AI.
